partial_result:
**Verdict: conditionally feasible on paper, unverified on GB10, and not a stronger *threat model* than hashing.** A read-only CUDA VMM owner can replace the two per-call 1.7 GB fingerprints with O(448) metadata checks plus one driver query, but only inside the same trust boundary the hashing already assumes. Nothing in NVIDIA's primary docs confirms that `CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READ` is honored on any device, let alone GB10, so the capability falsifier below must run before any design work.

## What the sources establish

- **VMM API shape is documented.** `cuMemCreate` makes an unmapped physical handle; `cuMemMap` places it in a `cuMemAddressReserve` range; mapping grants no access until `cuMemSetAccess`; teardown order is unmap, release, address-free ([driver VA group](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__VA.html), [Programming Guide VMM chapter](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/virtual-memory-management.html)). The guide mandates querying `CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_VIRTUAL_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT_SUPPORTED` first.
- **Read-only is declared, not demonstrated.** The enum lists `PROT_READ` as "make the address range read accessible" ([types page](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html)). Every NVIDIA example, including the [VMM blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/introducing-low-level-gpu-virtual-memory-management/), uses only `PROT_READWRITE`. Whether `cuMemSetAccess` with `PROT_READ` returns success, whether copy engines honor it, and whether it can be flipped after mapping are all unverified. `cuMemSetAccess` "exhibits synchronous behavior for most use cases" but does not synchronize prior work.
- **GB10 support is inferred only.** Driver on the box is 580.159.03 aarch64 with Torch 2.12.1+cu130. Third-party reports say PyTorch expandable segments work on GB10, which uses the same four VMM calls, but no source reports the attribute value.
- **Torch `.data` assignment is a metadata swap, not a byte write.** `VariableHooks::set_data` does `shallow_copy_from` of all non-autograd TensorImpl fields onto the same Python object ([variable.cpp v2.12.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.12.1/torch/csrc/autograd/variable.cpp)). So substitution changes `data_ptr`, shape, stride, or dtype, and is caught by metadata equality without any hash. It never touches protected bytes.
- **DLPack import wraps the pointer with no copy and ignores read-only.** `fromDLPackImpl` calls `at::from_blob` with a deleter that invokes the capsule's deleter when the storage dies, and never reads `flags` ([DLConvertor.cpp v2.12.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.12.1/aten/src/ATen/DLConvertor.cpp)). Torch's own docs warn that in-place ops on `from_dlpack` tensors write through ([torch 2.12 dlpack](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.12/dlpack.html)). Protection therefore must come from the GPU page table, not from DLPack.
- **A blocked write is a fail-stop, not a ValueError.** A store to a non-writable range "would generate a device fault as if you accessed invalid memory" (blog). That is sticky `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`: the process must be relaunched. Rejection becomes process death at the write instead of a caught exception at the next call. The current gates already treat mutation as FAIL, so this is acceptable only if the log captures exit code and error string.

## Smallest design that preserves current rejection

Load path (one-time, inside `load_inference`): query the VMM attribute and granularity via ctypes on the already-loaded `libcuda.so.1`; one `cuMemCreate(DEVICE)` sized to the 448-tensor packing at 512-byte offsets (the caching allocator's alignment, so cuBLAS heuristics see the same pointer alignment); copy each CPU tensor in with `cuMemcpyHtoD` under `PROT_READWRITE` straight from the existing `CheckpointPages` flow, so no transient `cudaMalloc` copy of the model exists; flip to `PROT_READ`; fingerprint once by DtoH readback against `vision_sha256` (the existing `fingerprint` already does `.cpu()`); build one DLPack capsule via `ctypes.pythonapi.PyCapsule_New` and `torch.from_dlpack`, then rebind each parameter with `torch.nn.Parameter(view, requires_grad=False)`, which shares storage. Keep `readout_sha256` and the `position_ids` buffer hashed per call unchanged. Per call, replace the two `encoder_facts` fingerprints with: object identity against recorded parameter objects, `data_ptr`, shape, stride, `storage_offset`, dtype, device, storage `data_ptr` and `nbytes` equal to the recorded VMM base, and `cuMemGetAccess` equal to `PROT_READ`. Release: after the existing weakref check proves the storages are dead, unmap, release, address-free in that order; the owner holds the CFUNCTYPE deleter alive until then. Pointer reuse is impossible while the owner holds the base tensor, because the range stays mapped. Memory bound is Torch peak plus the VMM range, rounded to granularity, reported separately because the caching allocator does not see it.

## Threat boundary, stated plainly

Any in-process code that can call `libcuda` can run `cuMemSetAccess(ptr, size, PROT_READWRITE)` on the same VA range with no handle. The hashing scheme is equally defeated by in-process native code that monkeypatches `require`. Both schemes protect against the public Torch API surface: `.data=`, `set_`, `copy_`, parameter replacement. PROT_READ is stronger inside that boundary because bytes cannot change at all, and strictly weaker outside it only in that a flip-write-flip leaves no trace, which hashing would catch at the next call. Say this in the frozen schema rather than claiming "physical immutability."

## Two falsifiers with exact stop rules

1. **CUDA capability, disposable, no Torch, no model.** Separate process, ctypes on `libcuda.so.1`, one allocation of the minimum granularity: attribute query, `cuMemCreate`, reserve, map, `SetAccess RW`, `HtoD` pattern, `SetAccess READ`, `GetAccess`, `DtoH` compare, then `cuMemcpyHtoD` to the range, then a one-thread kernel store via a tiny cubin, each followed by `cuCtxSynchronize`. Record cgroup `memory.current` before and after `cuMemCreate`. STOP if the attribute is 0, `SetAccess READ` returns non-success, `GetAccess` is not 1, the DtoH bytes differ, or either write path returns `CUDA_SUCCESS` after synchronize. Pass requires both writes to return an error. Expected exit is a sticky-error death; that is the pass signal, so the harness must capture the return codes before the context dies.
2. **Source-only ownership, CPU, Python 3.13.9 env, no GPU.** Build a two-parameter module whose tensors are `torch.frombuffer` views over a `PROT_READ` mmap, record the metadata predicate, then apply each public-API vector: `p.data = other`, `p.data = p.data.t()`, `p.set_(other)`, `module._parameters[name] = Parameter(other)`, `p.data = frombuffer(same mapping)`, `p.view(torch.int32)` rebinding, and `p.copy_(x)` in a subprocess. STOP if any vector changes the bytes the forward would read without tripping the predicate, or if the in-place subprocess exits 0. The same-mapping vector must pass with identical bytes, proving "same pointer, same bytes" is sound.

## Critical unknowns

- `PROT_READ` acceptance and copy-engine enforcement on GB10 with driver 580.159.03.
- Whether `cuMemCreate` device memory on unified LPDDR5X is charged to the 8 GiB cgroup. The existing 6.375 GB host peak with the model resident suggests not, but it is unmeasured.
- Whether a `cuMemSetAccess` flip after mapping is permitted at all; docs only show first-time grants.
- cuBLASLt kernel selection on Blackwell with 512-byte-aligned DLPack views versus caching-allocator pointers. The B1/B32 parity gate exists for exactly this, but it runs only after review.
- Fail-stop as rejection must be ruled acceptable by the frozen schema before measurement, because it changes the failure mode of every historical gate from exception to process death.

If falsifier 1 fails, the one equivalent alternative is a separate serving process that holds the weights and exposes only pixel-in, feature-out over a socket, so the Python authority never owns the bytes. That is a larger change and not recommended before the two cheap checks run.

1. **CUDA capability, disposable, no Torch, no model.** Separate process, ctypes on `libcuda.so.1`, one allocation of the minimum granularity: attribute query, `cuMemCreate`, reserve, map, `SetAccess RW`, `HtoD` pattern, `SetAccess READ`, `GetAccess`, `DtoH` compare, then `cuMemcpyHtoD` to the range, then a one-thread kernel store via a tiny cubin, each followed by `cuCtxSynchronize`. Record cgroup `memory.current` before and after `cuMemCreate`. STOP if the attribute is 0, `SetAccess READ` returns non-success, `GetAccess` is not 1, the DtoH bytes differ, or either write path returns `CUDA_SUCCESS` after synchronize. Pass requires both writes to return an error. Expected exit is a sticky-error death; that is the pass signal, so the harness must capture the return codes before the context dies.
2. **Source-only ownership, CPU, Python 3.13.9 env, no GPU.** Build a two-parameter module whose tensors are `torch.frombuffer` views over a `PROT_READ` mmap, record the metadata predicate, then apply each public-API vector: `p.data = other`, `p.data = p.data.t()`, `p.set_(other)`, `module._parameters[name] = Parameter(other)`, `p.data = frombuffer(same mapping)`, `p.view(torch.int32)` rebinding, and `p.copy_(x)` in a subprocess. STOP if any vector changes the bytes the forward would read without tripping the predicate, or if the in-place subprocess exits 0. The same-mapping vector must pass with identical bytes, proving "same pointer, same bytes" is sound.

## Critical unknowns

- `PROT_READ` acceptance and copy-engine enforcement on GB10 with driver 580.159.03.
- Whether `cuMemCreate` device memory on unified LPDDR5X is charged to the 8 GiB cgroup. The existing 6.375 GB host peak with the model resident suggests not, but it is unmeasured.
- Whether a `cuMemSetAccess` flip after mapping is permitted at all; docs only show first-time grants.
- cuBLASLt kernel selection on Blackwell with 512-byte-aligned DLPack views versus caching-allocator pointers. The B1/B32 parity gate exists for exactly this, but it runs only after review.
- Fail-stop as rejection must be ruled acceptable by the frozen schema before measurement, because it changes the failure mode of every historical gate from exception to process death.

If falsifier 1 fails, the one equivalent alternative is a separate serving process that holds the weights and exposes only pixel-in, feature-out over a socket, so the Python authority never owns the bytes. That is a larger change and not recommended before the two cheap checks run.
